tolerances.note: This batch is a ROUTING probe (which Julia solver ran), not a numerical-parity check, so no numeric tolerance applies to any case's point estimate or CI bound -- the pass/fail criterion is solver identity (route_tag) or, for the two LAMBDA-CI-UNSUPPORTED-METHOD-REJECT rows, whether an ArgumentError was raised.

known_findings.lambda_reject_validation_boundary: Empirically verified (see tools/core070_inference_batch.jl, CI-ROUTE-006/007): confint(fit, y; parm=..., method=<bad Symbol>) DOES raise ArgumentError('method must be :wald, :profile or :bootstrap') when the fit is an AGHQ Gaussian record (_has_gaussian_record(fit) == true; the validating branch is src/families/aghq_gaussian_fit.jl:202-221, reached via src/confint.jl:359-370). This validation is NOT reached for the plain (non-AGHQ) Gaussian fitter used by the sigma_B/sigma_W/sigma_phy buckets: src/families/aghq_gaussian_fit.jl:33-46 sets integration.data=nothing on the has_diag/K_W/K_phy/has_phy_unique ("structured") branch even when aghq is requested, so _has_gaussian_record is always false there and confint(fit,y;method=<anything>) silently falls through to the always-Wald 1-arg confint (src/confint.jl:369), ignoring `method` entirely. The manifest's LAMBDA-CI-UNSUPPORTED-METHOD-REJECT case happens to land on the validated (AGHQ-record) path because Lambda routing in this batch uses fixture A, so it is bucketed EXECUTABLE_NOW and passes; a hypothetical structured-fit reject case would not have found a validating call site. Recorded here so the boundary is not mistaken for a universal guarantee.
known_findings.derived_quantity_reject_spec_defect_reas: R's confint.gllvmTMB_multi validates the base method set with a single match.arg(method) call (z-confint-gllvmTMB.R:1716) AFTER intercepting icc/phylo_signal/communality/rho/proportion tokens, so an unsupported string like 'wald_asym' or 'bogus' reaches .confint_icc/.confint_phylo_signal/.confint_communality/.confint_rho/.confint_proportion as a literal method argument, which those functions individually reject with cli_abort. GLLVM.jl has no equivalent single call site: a caller selects the derived-quantity solver by which FUNCTION they call (communality_wald_ci vs GLLVM.profile_ci_derived vs GLLVM.bootstrap_ci_derived), not by passing a method string/symbol into one dispatcher. There is therefore no Julia call this case's own comparand ("a bogus method Symbol must raise a clear error") can be run against for these five quantities: the failure mode the R fixture is probing does not exist in Julia's function-per-method API design, by construction rather than by omission. This is a spec/comparand mismatch in the manifest row, not a defect in GLLVM.jl -- see LAMBDA-CI-UNSUPPORTED-METHOD-REJECT (CI-ROUTE-006/007) for the one case in this batch where a real method::Symbol call site (confint(fit,y;method=...)) does exist and is genuinely exercised.

rows.reason: R method='wald_asym' routes to loading_ci(method='wald_asym', loading_scale='standardized') with rho[trait,axis] parameter labels (a Fisher-z-flavoured *standardized*-loading Wald CI, distinct from the raw-scale wald route already covered by CI-ROUTE-003). GLLVM.jl has no standardized-loading/rho Wald CI entry point; confint()/profile_ci()/bootstrap_ci() only ever report Lambda_B on its raw (unstandardized) scale. Building this would require a new packed-theta closure for the standardized loading plus wiring it through the existing Fisher-z transformed-Wald machinery (src/confint_derived_wald.jl) -- that is new engine-adjacent surface, not something this batch's test code can supply on its own the way the communality/correlation/phylo_signal closures do (those already have an existing natural-scale analogue; standardized Lambda does not).

No `icc(fit)` point-estimate function exists in GLLVM.jl (grep of src/confint_derived.jl confirms only communality/proportions/correlation/phylo_signal are defined), and R's `extract_repeatability()` computes a specific combination of variance components (shared + unique-B over total, per z-confint-gllvmTMB.R's .confint_icc) that has no verified Julia formula to anchor a derived_fn closure on. Inventing one for this batch would be constructing a new, unverified quantity rather than exercising an existing surface -- exactly the engine-code line this task says not to cross. icc_wald_ci/profile_ci_derived/bootstrap_ci_derived exist and would ROUTE correctly once a grounded icc point-estimate is supplied; only that grounding is missing.
depends on the same missing icc point-estimate grounding as CI-ROUTE-008-011; without a real icc call site there is no route to probe rejection against.
